parts: A linear programming problem (LPP) maximises or minimises a linear objective function Z = ax + by subject to linear constraints (inequalities) and x, y ≥ 0. The variables x, y are the decision variables.

Name the quantities to be decided, write the objective (profit to maximise or cost to minimise), and turn each resource limit or requirement into an inequality. Percentages become decimals: 10% nitrogen in x kg gives 0.1x.

Draw each constraint as a line, shade the side that satisfies it, and find the feasible region common to all. The optimum of Z always occurs at a corner point of the feasible region (if it exists). Evaluate Z at every corner and pick the largest (max) or smallest (min) value. If two adjacent corners give the same optimum, every point on the segment joining them is optimal.
For an unbounded region, a minimum found at a corner is valid only if the half-plane Z < that value has no point in common with the region.
